text: When the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
Then the Philistines took the ark of God, carried it into the temple of Dagon, and set it up beside Dagon.
When the people of Ashdod rose early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and put him back in his place.

But when they rose early the following morning, there was Dagon again, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD, with his head and the palms of both his hands cut off, lying on the threshold. Only his body was left.

versions.text: But when they rose early the following morning, there was Dagon again, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD, with his head and both his hands broken off on the threshold. Only his trunk was left.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כְּרֻתוֹת means "cut off/severed" rather than "broken off," and כַּפּוֹת יָדָיו specifies the palms of his hands. "Trunk" is an interpretive rendering of the Hebrew, which simply says "only Dagon was left of him"; "body" is closer and reads more naturally aloud.

text: That is why to this day the priests of Dagon and all who enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.

The hand of the LORD lay heavy on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and struck them with tumors,<fn>The Hebrew term refers to painful swellings; the affliction may have been an outbreak of plague.</fn> both Ashdod and its territory.

versions.text: The hand of the LORD lay heavy on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and its territory.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote at the first occurrence of "tumors" would help hearers understand an unfamiliar term without interrupting the flow of the reading.

text: When the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us, for his hand is harsh against us and against Dagon our god."

So they sent word and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and asked, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" They answered, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be moved to Gath." So they moved the ark of the God of Israel.
But after they had moved it, the hand of the LORD was against that city, throwing it into a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, young and old, and tumors broke out on them.
So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. But as the ark of God entered Ekron, the people of Ekron cried out, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to us to kill us and our people!"

They sent word and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, "Send the ark of the God of Israel away. Let it return to its own place, so that it will not kill us and our people." For a deadly panic had fallen on the whole city; the hand of God lay very heavy there.
Those who did not die were struck with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.
